# tScrub

> tScrub is an open ITAD (IT asset disposition) platform built for compliance. It erases NVMe, SATA, and SCSI drives to NIST 800-88 Clear, Purge, and Destroy levels and produces a verifiable, signed chain-of-custody report — while triaging and grading every machine it boots on (hardware profile, battery health, display, and MDM or BIOS lock status) with a printable diagnostics report. Boot the ready-to-go appliance image from USB or PXE on hardware you already own.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tscrub.com/): Overview, value proposition, features, and audiences.
- [Compliance](https://tscrub.com/compliance): How each wipe method maps to NIST 800-88 Clear, Purge, and Destroy, with GDPR/HIPAA/ISO 27001 reporting.
- [Pricing](https://tscrub.com/pricing): Free licence, Pay-as-you-go credit packs from £1.80/device, Team £99 (100 credits), Enterprise £399 (500 credits), with shared organisations and seats; the Windows Autopilot (MDM) check is a paid feature (1 credit per check) — free licences are self-serve; paid licences are issued by tScrub.
- [Download](https://tscrub.com/download): The bootable appliance ISO, with a SHA-256 checksum for verification.
- [Docs](https://tscrub.com/docs): Building the appliance, booting from USB (Windows/macOS/Linux) or over the network (PXE), boot-time hardware triage and MDM/BIOS-lock detection, choosing a report destination (USB, FTP, or the tScrub dashboard), dashboard remote commands and organisations, and verifying signed reports.
- [Resources](https://tscrub.com/resources): Data erasure guides — standards, drive types, wipe methods, certificates of destruction, and a buyer's guide.
- [FAQ](https://tscrub.com/faq): Certification, running on your own hardware, and edge-case drive handling.
- [Certificates](https://tscrub.com/dashboard/certificates): Upload reports on the Media page, then select a Chain of Custody ID to generate one consolidated, printable Certificate of Destruction per job, and manage every certificate on your account. Page 1 states how the data was destroyed (method, NIST SP 800-88 level, technique, media disposition); Annex A carries the per-drive detail.
- [Attested destruction](https://tscrub.com/docs): assets that never ran the appliance (phones with soldered storage, machines that will not boot, sealed units, media a wipe cannot address) can be recorded by hand from the Add button on the Devices and Media pages, with type, make, model, serial, the reason for destruction rather than sanitisation, the method, and optionally vendor, date, witness and the vendor's evidence reference. Such items appear on the same certificate in their own section, every line qualified "operator-attested — not instrument-verified"; they are never counted as sanitised and no wipe result, NIST level or SMART data is attributed to them. The dashboard badges them Attested and reports how many of the total are attestations.
- [Devices](https://tscrub.com/dashboard/devices): Every machine that has booted tScrub — hardware profile (display, battery, CPU, RAM, BIOS, TPM, Secure Boot), MDM and BIOS lock status, online presence and LAN IP, and a printable ITAD diagnostics report PDF per device.
- [Media](https://tscrub.com/dashboard/drives): Upload reports and view erasure and pre/post-wipe SMART data for every storage medium — drives, SSDs and flash, including items recorded by operator attestation, which are badged Attested. Each medium's reports are listed under it, uploaded manually or pushed from an appliance.
- [Contact](https://tscrub.com/contact): Sales, support, and compliance enquiries.

## Key facts

- Supports NVMe (crypto, block, overwrite sanitise + format fallback), ATA (enhanced/standard secure erase), and SCSI sanitise.
- Removes HPA/DCO hidden areas before erasing (full native capacity) and verifies the wipe by re-reading sample sectors (sampled by default, full read-back opt-in).
- Handles SED/OPAL drives via PSID revert and detects BIOS Block SID lockdown (0x4286).
- Hardware triage & grading at boot: display panel (EDID), battery health/capacity, CPU spec, DIMMs, board serial, BIOS, TPM, Secure Boot, MACs, and storage controllers.
- Windows Autopilot MDM check run from the dashboard (Locked/Unlocked), BIOS password-lock detection, and remote commands — shut down, restart, stage a wipe, or clear a BIOS admin password on supported Dell, Lenovo and HP machines. The dashboard explains why a clear failed, and every command is listed in a per-device log and stamped with the chain of custody of the session that ran it.
- Team and Enterprise licences include a shared organisation with seats (2/10/50/100 across Free/Pay-as-you-go/Team/Enterprise) and a pooled credit balance for multiple operators.
- Printable two-page ITAD diagnostics report PDF per device (machine summary + storage inventory) from the Devices tab.
- Opt-in hardware self-tests (CPU arithmetic + per-drive short self-test).
- Every report carries a report_id (UUID) + digital_identifier (SHA-256) for tamper-evident audit proof.
- Chain-of-custody report (CSV) with COCID, system serials, and per-drive final status.
- Reports can be signed (SHA-256 + Ed25519) for verifiable proof of destruction.
- NIST 800-88 alignment, GDPR, HIPAA, ISO 27001.
- Selectable software-overwrite standards for drives without a firmware erase (zero, PRNG, DoD 5220.22-M, DoD Short, Gutmann, HMG IS5 Enhanced); the report records the standard (`OverwriteStandard`), pass count and engine version.
- Recorded verification technique per drive (`VerifyTechnique`): `sentinel` (planted sectors re-read and gone), `overwrite-sample` (N% of the address space read back as zero after a software overwrite, opt-in `--verify-coverage N`, `VerifyCoveragePct`), or `ce-exempt` (crypto erase; a content read-back proves nothing either way).
- The choice can be made on the appliance's triage screen (`m` cycles the standard, `p` the rounds), fixed per fleet with `tscrub_method=`/`tscrub_passes=`, or passed as `--method`/`--passes`.
- Bootable, inspectable appliance image; inspect every line of what runs.
- Triage-first boot: diagnostics + online heartbeat at boot; erasure starts on Shift+T from the triage screen.
- End-to-end loop: erase → signed report → PDF Certificate of Destruction with a verification QR (signed code checked at tscrub.com/verify-offline, record at tscrub.com/verify).
- Air-gapped certificate checking: the certificate QR carries a signed code checked on the device at tscrub.com/verify-offline, so an auditor with no network can confirm the certificate was issued by tScrub and not altered, against the published Ed25519 key.
- Every certificate is also issued as a signed machine-readable JSON-LD document (add &format=jsonld to the verification URL), so automated auditors can ingest and verify it without parsing the PDF.
- The customer (data controller) certifies their own destruction; tScrub supplies the signed, tamper-evident evidence.
- Open source (GPL-3.0), runs on your own hardware. Contrast: Blancco = closed, platform-only, enterprise quote; nwipe/DBAN = free ad-hoc overwrite, no signed reports or certificates.
